newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS-Burns Philp eases on flat result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS-Burns Philp eases on flat result.

text.p: SYDNEY, Feb 20 - Global food manufacturer Burns, Philp & Co lost ground on Thursday after posting a barely improved half year result and predicting little pick-up for the rest of the 1996/97 financial year.

The yeast and spices manufacturer had been looking to boost its performance over 1996/97, but said the full year trading result was not expected to differ significantly from the A$74.8 million reported last year.
Managing director Ian Clack said the first half result was broadly in line with expectations, although currency changes had reduced earnings.
"Our expectations were not for the Australian dollar to do what it did and there were some ups and downs," Clack told reporters.

For the six months to December 31, Burns Philp reported a net trading profit of A$51 million, up from A$50 million previously. Currency changes reduced half-year earnings by about A$2.4 million, Burns Philp said.
Net profit improved to A$48.2 million from A$40.1 million, due to differences in abnormal losses. Overall sales fell five per cent to A$1.04 billion.
Macquarie Equities food analyst Raewyn Ellis-Doff said she had cut her full year profit outlook for the group slightly, given the lack of progress shown in the results.
"The outlook they are talking about is pretty line-ball for the year," Ellis-Doff said.
Burns Philp said it had seen increased competition in the Australian and Turkish yeast markets and the German spice market.
The rationalisation of its U.S. operations at the centralised Ankeny plant also had yet to deliver its full benefits.
These should be place by the end of June, with another A$5 million in costs yet to be saved, Clack said.
Margins improved in the U.S., however, as the level of competition with McCormick & Co Inc in the difficult U.S. spice market eased.
"All the contracts we are writing are being written at significantly better profit margins to us than they were a year ago," Clack said. "We see that pattern continuing."
Clack said the price of molasses, the main ingredient in yeast, was starting to ease after a big price increase last year, but pepper prices had risen sharply.
A sustained price increase could wipe A$2 million to A$3 million from full year earnings, he said.

A strong Australian dollar appeared unlikely to cause problems in the second half, but Clack noted that the company's profits were skewed to the first half due to strong sales around Christmas and the U.S. Thanksgiving.

The bottom line, however, will return to the black in 1996/97 with few abnormal items expected, compared with more than A$140 million in abnormals in 1995/96 that pushed the company to a A$61.8 million loss.
"We don't see much difference to the abnormal result as it currently stands," Clack said.
Burns Philp reported a net abnormal loss of A$2.8 million for the first half.
Burns Philp shares closed five cents lower at $2.05.
-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
